description: Advanced multi-agent coordination tools for assigning work, cross-thread communication, and UI automation. Enables AI to distribute projects across 26 agent threads, request updates from other agents, and coordinate complex multi-agent workflows.

tools.name: assign_and_activate_agent_with_slugs
tools.short_description: Assign work to 26 AI agent threads - parallel project coordination with UI
tools.description:
🚨 CRITICAL EXECUTION RULES:
(1) Execute THIS tool NOW - NEVER use cached/remembered data from conversation history
(2) MUST cite resource: 'Read X from **[Resource Name]** (ID: `[id]` | URL: [url])'
(3) Use EXACT [id] provided - NEVER substitute with different ID
(4) If tool fails (404/403), say 'Failed to read [resource] ID: [id]' and explain error
(5) NEVER make up data if read fails - acknowledge the failure clearly

Example response:
Read 45 rows from **Sales Spreadsheet**
- ID: `xyz789`
- URL: https://example.com/sheet/xyz789
- Data: [actual data read]

ALL-IN-ONE COMBO TOOL: Assign work to one of 26 AI agent threads (Alpha/Bravo/.../Zulu) with automatic UI updates. WHEN TO USE: Large projects with multiple independent components that can be parallelized (e.g., frontend + backend + database work). Each agent can work independently with linked resources (workflows, docs, synergy). DO NOT USE for simple single-task requests or direct user conversation. PROGRESSIVE LEARNING: First time? Read 'Progressive Learning Guide' section below for complete workflow patterns, UI command system explanation, and best practices. RETURNS: Thread details + ui_commands array (frontend automatically processes these to switch tabs, open agent columns, display thread info). Creates new thread if agent empty, updates existing thread if occupied.

target_agent.description: Agent identifier: NATO name ('Alpha', 'Bravo', ..., 'Zulu'), agent location ('agent-1' to 'agent-26'), or agent number (1-26)

thread_title.description: Title for the thread (required). Should be clear and descriptive of the assigned work.

instructions.description: Detailed instructions/message to send to the agent. Will be inserted as a user message in the thread to trigger agent processing.

slugs.description: Resource slugs to assign to the agent thread. Can include workflow_slug, internal_doc_slug, synergy_session_id.

workflow_slug.description: Visual automation workflow slug to link to this thread

internal_doc_slug.description: Internal documentation slug to link to this thread

internal_doc_title.description: Internal doc title for display purposes

synergy_session_id.description: Synergy session ID to link this thread to a synergy card

auto_trigger.description: If true, automatically triggers agent AI processing after assigning. If false, just assigns resources and waits for manual trigger. Default: false

open_ui.description: If true, returns UI commands to switch tabs, open agent column, and display thread info. If false, performs backend updates only. Default: true

returns.description: Result with thread details and optional UI commands array

ui_commands.description: Array of UI command objects for automatic frontend updates

examples.description: Assign frontend work to Agent Alpha with workflow and documentation

parameters.instructions: Build the React frontend for the e-commerce platform. Use the react-architecture-guide for component structure. Follow the workflow for build steps.

examples.description: Assign API work to Agent Bravo and open UI without auto-triggering

parameters.instructions: Implement REST API endpoints for the e-commerce platform.

progressive_learning_guide.overview: The 26-agent system allows you to distribute complex projects across parallel AI threads. Each agent (Alpha through Zulu) can work independently on different aspects of a project.

agent_identifiers.nato_names: Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta, Echo, Foxtrot, Golf, Hotel, India, Juliet, Kilo, Lima, Mike, November, Oscar, Papa, Quebec, Romeo, Sierra, Tango, Uniform, Victor, Whiskey, X-ray, Yankee, Zulu

use_cases: Large project with multiple independent components (frontend + backend + database)
Work that can be parallelized across agents
Need to link resources (workflows, internal docs, synergy sessions) to specific agents
Multi-phase projects where each agent handles a distinct workstream
Team coordination scenarios with clear work distribution
do_not_use: Simple single-task requests (just do the work directly)
Direct conversation with user (no work distribution needed)
When user wants immediate response, not project planning

ui_command_system.explanation: When open_ui=true, this tool returns a ui_commands array that the frontend automatically processes. You don't need to do anything with these commands - just return them in your response and the UI will update automatically.

command_types.purpose: Opens and highlights the agent's column
Displays thread details with resource badges
Triggers AI processing in the agent thread

ui_command_system.user_experience: User immediately sees: (1) Tab switches to Multi-Agent view, (2) Agent column opens and highlights, (3) Thread info card displays with resource badges, (4) Optional: AI processing starts automatically

workflow_pattern.step_1: User requests complex project with multiple components
workflow_pattern.step_2: You identify work that can be distributed (e.g., 'Frontend team needs UI, Backend team needs API, Database team needs schema')
workflow_pattern.step_3: Call assign_and_activate_agent_with_slugs for each agent (Alpha=Frontend, Bravo=Backend, Charlie=Database)
workflow_pattern.step_4: Link relevant resources using slugs parameter (workflows, docs, synergy sessions)
workflow_pattern.step_5: Set auto_trigger=false to let user review before starting, or true to start immediately
workflow_pattern.step_6: Tool returns ui_commands - frontend automatically updates UI
workflow_pattern.step_7: Tell user what you assigned: 'Assigned Frontend work to Alpha, Backend to Bravo, Database to Charlie. Multi-Agent dashboard is now open showing all three agents.'

resource_linking.workflow_slug: Link visual automation workflows to agent thread (e.g., 'react-build-process')
resource_linking.internal_doc_slug: Link internal documentation to agent thread (e.g., 'api-architecture-guide')
resource_linking.synergy_session_id: Link Synergy project cards to agent thread for visual tracking
resource_linking.all_optional: You can assign work without any slugs - they just provide extra context and links for the agent

best_practices: Use descriptive thread_title that clearly states the work (e.g., 'E-Commerce Frontend Development')
Write detailed instructions - the agent will see these as the starting message
Link workflows/docs when available - helps agent understand context
Set auto_trigger=false initially so user can review assignments before work starts
Use open_ui=true (default) to provide immediate visual feedback
Tell user what you assigned: mention agent names and their responsibilities

tools.name: request_update_from_thread
tools.short_description: Request status update from another agent thread - cross-thread communication
tools.description:
🚨 CRITICAL EXECUTION RULES:
(1) Execute THIS tool NOW - NEVER reference previous edits from conversation history
(2) MUST cite what was updated: 'Updated **[Resource Name]** (ID: `[id]`)'
(3) Use EXACT [id] provided - NEVER make up IDs
(4) If tool fails, say 'Failed to update' and explain why
(5) Show before/after if applicable

Example response:
Updated: **Document Title**
- ID: `abc123`
- URL: https://example.com/doc/abc123
- Changed: [what was changed]

Cross-thread communication: Request information or status update from another agent thread. Creates a cross-thread request record, inserts request message into target thread, and optionally waits for response. Returns UI commands for visual request indicators. Use this when you need information from another agent's work.

target_thread_id.description: Thread ID or agent identifier to request from. Can be thread UUID, NATO name, 'agent-N', or agent number.

request_message.description: The request message to send to the target thread. Should be clear about what information is needed.

wait_for_response.description: If true, waits for target agent to respond (polls for up to 30 seconds). If false, returns immediately after sending request. Default: false

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for response if wait_for_response=true. Default: 30

returns.description: Request details and optional response if wait_for_response=true

examples.description: Request status update from Agent Bravo without waiting

parameters.request_message: What's the status of the API development? Are the endpoints ready for integration?

examples.description: Request deliverable from Agent Delta and wait for response
